h1: Ocean Animals Word Search (Free Printable Sea Life Puzzle)
intro: Print a free ocean animals word search with 22 sea creatures, from tiny seahorses to enormous whales. It supports a unit on the ocean, a trip to an aquarium or a quiet afternoon at the beach.
itemsNote: The 22 words above are loaded. Pick a smaller set to match the animals you will see on an aquarium visit.

sections.heading: How to use this word search with an ocean unit
body: Ocean animals fascinate children, and the unusual names stick when they are found in a grid. This puzzle works as a hook at the start of a unit or a review at the end.

1. Ask the class to name an ocean animal before handing out the sheets, and see which ones appear in the list.
2. Solve the puzzle and put a star by every animal that has a shell, fins or tentacles.
3. Pick one animal and look up where it lives: near the shore, in the open ocean or in the deep.
4. Finish with a drawing of an ocean scene with every animal in the right zone.

> Some animals in this list, such as the manatee, are mammals or turtles that breathe air. [NOAA Fisheries](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species-directory) has species profiles you can use for facts.

sections.heading: Three ocean variations
body:
* **Sort by body type.** After solving, children sort the animals into fish, mammals, shellfish and soft-bodied animals.
* **Mystery creature.** One child describes an animal without naming it, and the others guess and find it in the grid.
* **Deep sea mural.** Each child draws one animal, labels it with a word from the list, and the class assembles a wall mural.

sections.heading: Tips for teachers and parents
body: Spelling anemone and narwhal can trip up even older children. Say each word aloud when it is found, so the sound and spelling connect.
Check pictures online or in a book for any animal the children do not know. A quick look at a seahorse or a pufferfish brings the word to life.

sections.heading: Printing tips for sea life
body: Print in black and white and let children color a border of waves around the sheet. Pale blue paper is nice, but keep it light.
The 15 by 15 grid gives plenty of room for sea turtle, blue whale and clownfish. For small hands on a car trip, drop to 12 by 12 and pick 12 words.

faq.q: What age is the ocean animals word search for?
faq.a: It suits ages 6 to 10. Younger children can use the easy setting and a shorter list.
No. The list includes mammals like dolphins and manatees, mollusks like octopus and squid, and animals like crabs and starfish. This can start a good discussion about how to group animals.

faq.q: Can I use it for a beach vacation?
faq.a: Yes. Print a small copy and tuck it in a beach bag, then tick off any animal you see.
